summary: Unexpected ordering and idempotency anomalies when sending multiplexed batched tool invocations across sharded clients
description:
Issue summary:
VeloxApps reports that when they multiplex multiple client shards into a single batched request (they multiplex client connections for throughput), some tool/function invocations are executed out of the expected order and occasionally re-run despite using an idempotency token per logical action. This manifests sporadically under load and after a scheduler rebalance.

Impact:
- Multiple customers of VeloxApps observe transactional side-effects (webhook posts, DB writes) happening in the wrong order or being processed twice, causing inconsistent application state.
- Occurs intermittently (~0.3% of requests) but affects high-value workflows; customer flagged as P1 due to business impact.

Environment details:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated pool) in us-east.
- SDKs: python 1.4.2, go 0.9.8.
- Pattern: 8 client shards multiplexed via a custom gateway that merges requests into a batch with per-invocation idempotency_token and sequence_index metadata.
- Model: rw-open-7b-v1 with KV cache enabled and batching window set to 50ms.

Expected behavior:
- Each logical tool invocation should be executed at most once (idempotent) and, when sequence_index is provided, should preserve ordering across invocations from the same logical session.

Observed behavior:
- Some invocations are processed twice despite identical idempotency_token.
- Sequence ordering is violated: later sequence_index gets executed before an earlier one for a small subset of multiplexed batches.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Spin up dedicated pool stub in us-east and route 8 client shards through a local gateway that multiplexes.
2) Send a batch of 120 short inference requests that include: model call + tool invocation (webhook POST) with idempotency_token and sequence_index.
3) Simulate scheduler rebalance by draining one serving worker during the run.
4) Observe webhook endpoints for duplicate posts and compare sequence_index ordering.

Logs (snippets provided):
- Gateway merge log shows single batched request id: batch-20260310-09:22:14 with 120 records.
- Serving runtime trace: "worker-7 accepted batch-20260310-09:22:14" then "worker-3 recovered KV cache for shard 4 and re-enqueued 7 ops".
- Webhook logs: duplicate POST for invocation token idemp-9a1b, timestamps 09:22:14.814 and 09:22:14.923.

Attachments provided by customer: merging gateway logs, serving traces, webhook endpoint headers.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Triage by Support (Maya): Collected logs and verified customer's dedicated pool id. Reproduced single duplicate in internal load test using customer's gateway pattern but only after simulated worker drain.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Rafael): Hypothesis A: During rebalancing, some in-flight batched subrequests are resubmitted by the scheduler when KV cache miss occurs; idempotency tokens may not be propagated to the resubmitted execution path due to an edge case in the batch splitter.
Hypothesis B: Multiplexing layer sets sequence_index but uses per-shard ephemeral id namespace which collides after requeue leading to double-exec detection not matching.
    Action: Add deterministic logging for idempotency_token at batch boundary and instrument batch-split/merge code paths.

2026-03-12 - Eng instrumentation: Found that when a batch is split into two worker assignments (for parallelism), the batch splitter was not always forwarding the original idempotency_token through the worker-queued tasks when a split occurs post-KV-cache-lookup. This causes the re-enqueued task to have a blank token which bypasses idempotency dedupe downstream.

2026-03-12 - Additional note: Sequence ordering violation appears correlated with split+requeue: requeued tasks are appended to the end of the target worker's queue without preserving original sequence_index ordering when cross-worker reshuffle occurs.

2026-03-12 - Customer note: Their gateway uses a custom header X-Session-Seq; confirmed that it maps to sequence_index but the multiplexer translates it to an internal monotonic per-batch counter that can reset during rebalance.

2026-03-13 - Priority decision: Treat as Sev1 for VeloxApps (P1). Engineering to implement a short-term mitigation (ensure idempotency_token is copied on split) and a medium-term fix (stronger invariants in batch splitter to preserve sequence_index ordering across requeue).
comments: 2026-03-10 - VeloxApps (Arjun Patel): We're seeing intermittent duplicates and bad order after rolling out a gateway optimization; happy to provide traffic replay. Impacting payment webhook ordering.
2026-03-10 - Support (Maya Chen): Thanks Arjun — we've opened SUP-81234 and requested logs + reproduction steps. Assigned Rafael from runtime eng to investigate.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Rafael Ortega): Can you confirm whether the idempotency_token is present in batch-level logs for re-enqueued tasks? Also, any chance the customer's gateway rewrites headers during multiplexing?
2026-03-11 - VeloxApps (Arjun): Gateway preserves cookies/headers; we attach idempotency_token in the body metadata, not headers. We'll send a traffic dump.

2026-03-12 - Eng (Rafael): We instrumented the splitter and confirmed tokens are sometimes lost when splitting for parallel workers. Working on a hotfix to copy token metadata explicitly on split. Will test on staging with simulated rebalance.

2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): Hotfix deployed to staging; please test and let us know if duplicates/order anomalies persist. We'll schedule a maintenance window to push to customer's dedicated pool if green.
resolution_notes:
2026-03-14 - Hotfix applied (serving runtime): Ensure idempotency_token and sequence_index are propagated on any batch split and when enqueuing requeued tasks. This prevents blank tokens from bypassing deduplication.
Rollout: Canary in staging -> limited rollout to 10% of production workers -> full rollout to dedicated pools after 24h verification.

Mitigation recommended to customer: Gatekeeper pattern — add server-side confirmation endpoint for side-effecting tools so a second identical POST is safely ignored until dedupe window expires. Also update gateway to include idempotency_token in top-level batch metadata (already recommended).

Follow-ups: Create a unit test for batch splitter invariants (idempotency_token and sequence ordering across requeue). Add a monitoring alert on duplicate tool invocations per-token > 0.05% over a 5m window. Owner: Rafael Ortega. Target completion: 2026-03-21.
